lesson.title: Reviewer Judgment Framework
lesson.summary: Teach reviewers how to compare interpretations, judge evidence sufficiency, calibrate confidence, resolve disagreement, justify narrative outcomes, and reach a final decision.
learningObjectives: Calibrate confidence to the available support.
Use narrative justification when the story changes the outcome.
Produce a final reviewer decision only after the full judgment process.

concepts.title: Competing Interpretations
concepts.summary: More than one valid reading exists and the reviewer must compare them.

concepts.title: Evidence Sufficiency
concepts.summary: The reviewer decides whether the evidence is enough for a conclusion.

concepts.title: Confidence Calibration
concepts.summary: The reviewer adjusts confidence to match evidence quality and uncertainty.

concepts.title: Reviewer Disagreement
concepts.summary: Different reviewers may legitimately disagree and the difference must be recorded.

concepts.title: Narrative Justification
concepts.summary: The story context changes or explains the reviewer outcome.

concepts.title: Final Reviewer Decision
concepts.summary: The combined judgment that resolves evidence, context, disagreement, and confidence.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: List the competing readings before choosing one.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must cite literal evidence.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Separate strong support from weak support.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must identify the strongest support.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Confidence must follow the strength of evidence and the amount of contradiction.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must reflect corroboration or uncertainty.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Capture legitimate disagreement instead of hiding it.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must explain why disagreement exists.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Does the narrative justify the outcome?
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: The story may change the reviewer result even when the line looks harmful.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must use story context.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Finalize only after evidence, context, disagreement, and confidence are resolved.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must state the final judgment.

examples: Two plausible readings exist, so the reviewer compares both before deciding.
A later sentence makes one reading weaker and another reading stronger.
The reviewer keeps the case as review until the evidence becomes sufficient.
A narrative explanation changes the final outcome.
counterExamples: Picking the first plausible reading without comparison.
Pretending reviewer disagreement does not exist.
Finalizing the decision before narrative justification is checked.
exceptions: quotation must be checked before judgment
historical narration may change the outcome
fiction may require a different judgment path
dream and flashback may alter the final reading

minimum: At least one literal clue must exist in the chunk.
The reviewer must identify the competing readings or the reason the reading is uncertain.
strong: More than one clue points toward the same interpretation.
Context and later text agree with the leading reading.
weak: A reading that remains plausible but unresolved.
insufficient: A final answer before context is checked.
confidenceGuidance: High confidence when the scene clearly resolves the dispute.
Medium confidence when competing readings remain partly open.
Low confidence when evidence is weak or contradictory.
Review required when the narrative has not yet justified the result.

conceptRelationships.note: Comparing readings comes before checking sufficiency.
Confidence explains why reviewers may disagree.
Disagreement may be resolved by narrative justification.
Narrative justification leads into the final decision.

glossaryReferences.note: The framework ends in a final reviewer decision.
The reviewer asks whether the evidence is enough.
The story may justify the outcome.

reportTemplates.recommendationTemplate: If the evidence is insufficient, keep the case in review and record the disagreement.
